title: Introduction
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter
coreMove: Separate observable behavior, motive story, and repeated pattern before judging anyone, starting with your own blindness.
sourcePressure: The frame chapter argues that motives hide beneath stories, self-love distorts self-knowledge, social life rewards masks, and the first honest subject is yourself.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Turning the opening into a generic warning that people are complicated instead of a disciplined method for reading motives while auditing yourself.

hook: a generic "people are not rational" opener for Introduction
opening with a definition of the law
starting with a vague office conflict
counterintuition: the obvious lesson is wrong because people are complicated
you think this is about others, but it is about you
the safest move is simply to be more self-aware
tryThisNow: pause and reflect for sixty seconds
write down three things you noticed
take a deep breath before reacting

exampleSpecs.domain: a city permit counter where a new inspector is judging a charming contractor
exampleSpecs.audience: a public employee learning to read motive without cynicism
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a rushed approval creates a costly zoning mess
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the inspector lays the contractor's three prior resubmission dates beside today's polished packet, then delays approval until the pattern speaks louder than the smile
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stamped permit packet fanned across a scratched service counter

exampleSpecs.domain: a community choir audition where a director mistakes nervous stiffness for arrogance
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer leader sorting talent from first impressions
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the best alto gets dismissed before anyone hears her second song
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director records first impression notes, then crosses them against callback behavior and catches the original motive story shrinking
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a folding music stand with one penciled score clipped open

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospital discharge desk where siblings argue over a parent's care plan
exampleSpecs.audience: a mediator trying to keep family history from swallowing current facts
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether old resentment derails a safe discharge
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the mediator repeats only the observable request, then asks each sibling what pattern would prove neglect rather than fear
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a plastic folder of discharge papers under fluorescent light

exampleSpecs.domain: a minor-league scouting meeting after one bad at-bat
exampleSpecs.audience: a scout under pressure to decide if a prospect lacks discipline
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a player is written off because one ugly swing felt decisive
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the scout replays six plate appearances on a tablet and marks the pattern before naming the player's character
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a tablet paused on a third-strike swing

exampleSpecs.domain: a neighborhood mutual-aid intake call with a caller who sounds evasive
exampleSpecs.audience: a coordinator deciding whether caution has become contempt
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a household loses help because tone is mistaken for motive
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coordinator writes down the exact evasions, then lists two noncharacter explanations before deciding what to ask next
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a headset coiled beside an intake form

exampleSpecs.domain: a boutique hiring panel seduced by a polished portfolio
exampleSpecs.audience: a founder who tends to confuse presentation with reliability
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the first hire becomes a chronic execution problem
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the founder predicts the portfolio star will be strongest, then checks reference behavior under missed deadlines and watches charm lose authority
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a glossy portfolio sleeve beside a plain reference transcript

skillTargets: separate behavior from assigned motive in ambiguous interactions
use repeated patterns rather than first impressions
apply the lens to the reader before diagnosing another person

tryThisNowSpec: Take one judgment you made today and write three columns: what you actually saw, the story you added, and the pattern you would need before trusting it.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm — a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
